statement: Engines did not fail but experienced unexplained speed issues during the journey.
source_context: *"No. Not fail. Thrust normal. But speed…not increase."*

statement: Rocky was dumbfounded by relativity.
source_context: Rocky was dumbfounded by relativity.

statement: Rocky accepts that the universe uses rules more complicated than visible.
source_context: He doesn’t like it, but he accepts that the universe uses rules that are much more complicated than we can see.

statement: Rocky is an engineer who efficiently produces chain links using xenonite.
source_context: Rocky cranked out links as fast as xenonite would set. It was a good system—one with a geometric progression of results.

statement: Rocky believes the ship does not touch the air, despite heat transfer.
source_context: *"Ship no touch air,"* Rocky says. *"Why is ship hot, question?"

statement: Rocky designed a sampler probe with a pressure sensor and temperature control system.
source_context: He also added a thermometer and heater in there. Once the sampler seals, the heater will maintain whatever temperature the air inside started at.

statement: Rocky does not grasp how heat affects the ship's cooling system.
source_context: *"Astrophage absorb heat. We safe,"* Rocky says.

statement: Rocky assumes the ship is Astrophage-cooled and therefore safe from extreme temperatures.
source_context: *"Astrophage absorb heat. We safe,"* Rocky says.

statement: Rocky uses a camera system to monitor the probe's status in real-time.
source_context: The Life Support panel comes up on my main screen, unprompted. EXTERNAL TEMPERATURE EXTREME, it warns.

statement: Rocky does not fully comprehend the physics of orbital gravity and weightlessness.
source_context: *"You ship is Astrophage-cooled, question?"* Yes. Astrophage cools ship.

statement: Rocky understands the relationship between engine tilt and forward motion in space.
source_context: The *H* Mary isn’t falling anymore. The engines hold us up in the sky and our tilt makes us scooch forward at 127 meters per second.

statement: Rocky believes he cannot make a spool big enough and strong enough to bring up the entire 10-kilometer chain.
source_context: Rocky informed me he’d never be able to make a spool big enough and strong enough to bring up the entire 10-kilometer length.

statement: Rocky believed the sampler could climb the chain but later dismissed the idea as too risky.
source_context: Rocky had a pretty clever thought: The sampler could climb the chain when it was done. But after some experimenting he ditched the idea. He said the risks just weren’t worth it.

statement: Rocky designed a special winch for retrieving the chain.
source_context: I grab a special winch Rocky designed and attach it to my suit’s tool belt.

statement: Rocky believes the chain's trap links can be separated by the winch without manual sealing.
source_context: It’s extremely unlikely that random movement would separate the links. But the winch is deliberately designed to do just that.

statement: Rocky misunderstands the ship's thrusting behavior, as he does not know what causes the sudden movement.
source_context: *“I not know. Ship move. Sudden.”*

statement: Rocky knows the chain is 10 kilometers long and contains a sample container with potential salvation.
source_context: I know it will take quite a while to pull up this whole chain, but I have to be ready for the sampler.

statement: Rocky believes the ship was made to handle acceleration and can endure similar forces from gravity.
source_context: *“Agree.”* But that bothers me in the back of my mind. This ship was *made* for acceleration.

statement: Rocky explains how to adhere the xenonite square to the hull using his detailed knowledge.
source_context: Rocky grabs several of his handholds for support. *“We have sampler. We leave now.”*

statement: Rocky misunderstands the ship's structural integrity under gravity, as he does not recognize the hull bending.
source_context: *“All around,”* he says. *“But loudest at starboard dormitory wall segment. It bending inward.”*

statement: Rocky learns about the ship's unexpected thrusting behavior and its potential to capsize.
source_context: *“Get inside fast fast fast!”* The horizon rises in my view. The *Hail Mary* isn’t maintaining her angle anymore.

statement: Rocky uses a textured screen to view camera feeds.
source_context: *“Screens flash many colors!”* he yells over the din. He points his camera here and there, watching the feed on his textured screen.

statement: Rocky believes the ship's hull is bending inward due to gravitational forces.
source_context: *“All around,”* he says. *“But loudest at starboard dormitory wall segment. It bending inward.”*

statement: Rocky does not understand the ship's structural limits or its ability to handle acceleration forces.
source_context: But that bothers me in the back of my mind. This ship was *made* for acceleration. It endured four years at 1.5 g’s. Surely it can handle this similar force? Something doesn’t add up.

statement: Rocky assumes the ship's engines are off when they are not, leading to confusion about thrust vectors.
source_context: *“Thrust continues,”* Rocky quavers. [After jettisoning fuel bays]

statement: The narrator learns that the ship's hull can melt due to heat conduction, not just Astrophage properties.
source_context: I *know* the fuel bay I jettisoned was in the affected area... [Realizes] the heat from Adrian’s infrared light caused the hull to melt.

statement: Rocky uses echolocation to sense the entire ship, including non-habitable areas like fuel tanks.
source_context: *“Yes yes yes!”* Rocky says, cheering me on. [After jettisoning fuel bays]

statement: The narrator learns that Astrophage absorbs energy and momentum from expelled fuel, creating chaotic thrust.
source_context: It’s a chaotic, sputtering explosion... [Explanation of Astrophage behavior]

statement: The narrator initially believes the ship's structural integrity is compromised due to gravity alone, ignoring the role of Astrophage.
source_context: The groaning of the ship has stopped... [Realizes the issue stems from Astrophage propulsion]

statement: Rocky believes he must save Earth and Erid
source_context: *"Save…Earth…Save…Erid…"* he quavers. Then he slumps down.

statement: The narrator misunderstands Rocky's location as being in the control room instead of his compartment
source_context: He’s in the control room! Not in his compartment. He’s in the control room!

statement: Rocky learns that mechanical suffocation is a method used by boa constrictors to kill prey
source_context: My lungs, now full of carbon dioxide, panic. But the adrenaline rush doesn’t give me the strength I need to escape. It just keeps me awake so I can experience death in more detail. Thanks, adrenal glands.

statement: The force felt in a centrifuge is inverse to the square of the radius.
source_context: The force you feel in a centrifuge is inverse to the square of the radius.

statement: Extending cables from 20 meters to 75 meters reduces centrifugal force to one-fourteenth.
source_context: I don’t know how much force I was dealing with before, but now it’s one-fourteenth as much as it was.

statement: The centrifuge does not rotate the crew compartment to face inward.
source_context: The centrifuge pushes everything toward the nose of the crew compartment. The lab is "up" from me now...

statement: Eridian biology equates cessation of movement with death.
source_context: How can I tell if an Eridian is dead? When Rocky sleeps all movement stops. But that’s also presumably what happens when an Eridian dies.

statement: Rocky weighs 200 pounds at half gravity (400 pounds at full gravity).
source_context: I did lift him, however briefly. It felt like 200 pounds. Thank god we’re in one-half gravity.

statement: The crew compartment's rotation controls are unknown to the narrator.
source_context: I don’t know where the manual controls for crew-compartment rotation are.

statement: Ammonia exposure causes severe respiratory and chemical burns.
source_context: Blazing-hot ammonia floods the airlock... My lungs feel like a hundred knives are having a dance-off.

statement: The ship's status (orbit or escape) is unknown to the narrator.
source_context: The ship is either in a stable orbit or we escaped Adrian’s gravity entirely.

statement: I know the very basics of Eridian biology.
source_context: I know the very basics of Eridian biology. That doesn’t make me a doctor.

statement: When severely wounded, an Eridian body will shut down so it can try to work on everything at once.
source_context: I don’t remember everything he told me, but at least I took copious notes. When severely wounded, an Eridian body will shut down so it can try to work on everything at once.

statement: Rocky’s radiator is made of deoxidized metal alloys.
source_context: The capillaries in Rocky’s radiator are made of deoxidized metal alloys, which he designed to handle the heat.

statement: Rocky designed the sampler to open when pressure matches Adrian’s atmosphere.
source_context: Rocky had the foresight to put readouts on the sampler so he could monitor the pressure. The little valves opened when the pressure matched Adrian’s atmosphere.

statement: Eridian biology uses mercury-based blood and capillaries for heat exchange.
source_context: I think I should let Rocky’s body heal itself as much as possible. If it can, it will. But if not... In ours, it makes a perfect tinderbox.

statement: Rocky has carapace vents that function similarly to human respiratory orifices.
source_context: I think they all lead to the same organ—like a human’s mouth and nose do. Multiple orifices for redundancy and safety.

statement: Rocky is stationary and unresponsive, indicating no immediate threat.
source_context: Rocky still hasn’t moved. No surprise there.

statement: Rocky’s carapace vents release black smoke as a result of internal combustion or debris.
source_context: Rocky’s carapace vents belch out black smoke. The nasty dust and debris that built up when he was on fire.

statement: Ammonia is clear, so the high-pressure air jet’s target location cannot be visually confirmed.
source_context: I have no idea where it’s going.

statement: Human light sense is very useful.
source_context: *"Human light sense very useful."*

statement: The black substance coming from Rocky's radiator is soot.
source_context: *"Black substance is not soot. My body make this. It cover damage while body repairs."*

statement: Blowing air into his radiator vents removes harmful substances.
source_context: *"You almost kill me."*

statement: Rocky can create a vacuum chamber to store Adrian life without air exposure.
source_context: *"I made device now to collect sample from inside and not let you air in."*

statement: Humans are stupid when they need sleep or take medicine.
source_context: *"You should sleep. You are stupid."*

statement: Both species evolved to perceive sounds, so overlapping frequency ranges is expected.
source_context: *"Useful trait. Both evolve. Not surprising."*

statement: Rocky knows about storing Adrian's life in a device.
source_context: *"I go to lab to see device that store Adrian life."

statement: Rocky explains the function of a vacuum chamber for sample collection.
source_context: *"I go to lab to see device that store Adrian life... seal it and collect samples."

statement: Rocky believes Eridians have a wider range of hearing frequencies than humans.
source_context: *"I do hear much higher frequency and much lower frequency."

statement: Rocky misunderstands human cognition, equating math with procedural tasks rather than thinking.
source_context: *"Math is not thinking. Math is procedure."

statement: Rocky believes both humans and Eridians are willing to die for their people.
source_context: *"You and me both willing to die for our people."

statement: Rocky accepts the theory that gravity influences animal speed and intelligence evolution.
source_context: *"Gravity is what determines how fast an animal can run... I accept this."

statement: Rocky believes leaving samples at human room temperature is reckless, using terms like 'reckless,' 'idiot,' and 'irresponsible.'
source_context: Rocky admonished me for leaving the sample at (human) room temperature for so long. He had a lot to say on that subject, actually. We had to add "reckless," "idiot," "foolish," and "irresponsible" to our shared vocabulary just so he could fully express his opinion on the matter.

statement: Rocky misunderstands human physiology, believing painkillers are necessary for the narrator's condition.
source_context: Rocky refused to give me the box I’m using until I slept three times without using the drugs. My arm hurts so bad right now, but he’s got a point.

statement: Rocky believes oxygen is dangerous due to his past injury, despite the narrator's clarification that the experiment uses carbon dioxide and nitrogen.
source_context: *"Can explode."* I pull my goggles off and look up at him. "There’s no oxygen in this experiment. Calm down." *"Yes. Calm."*

statement: Rocky learns to name the predator 'Taumoeba' based on the narrator's explanation of its origin.
source_context: *"Earth culture. You find. You name. What is name of predator, question?"* I... "Taumoeba, I guess."

statement: Rocky believes Taumoeba are 'the savior of Earth and Erid,' implying a belief in their significance.
source_context: *"Happy happy happy!"* he says. *"Now you name."*... "Taumoeba, I guess." Taumoeba. The savior of Earth and Erid.

statement: Rocky misunderstands the narrator's use of human cultural terms like 'rancher' and 'bolo tie,' assuming a role for Taumoeba.
source_context: I should have a bolo tie. Maybe a cowboy hat. Because I’m a rancher now. And I’m running about 50 million head of Taumoeba on my ranch.

statement: Oxygen is dangerous because his internal organs caught fire.
source_context: *"Oxygen dangerous." He’s been a little edgy since his internal organs caught fire.

statement: Threeworld's atmosphere is 84% carbon dioxide, 8% nitrogen, 4% sulfur dioxide, and trace gases.
source_context: According to Rocky, it’s 84 percent carbon dioxide, 8 percent nitrogen, 4 percent sulfur dioxide, and a bunch of trace gases.

statement: Threeworld's temperature at 0.02 atmosphere altitude is -82 degrees Celsius.
source_context: *"Minus eighty-two degrees of Celsius."

statement: Eridians lack ancient planetary naming traditions and only use designations like 'Planet Three'.
source_context: The Eridians don’t have a name for it, even in their own language. Just a designation: 'Planet Three.' They didn’t have ancient people looking up at astronomical bodies...

statement: Oxygen is dangerous and could cause explosions.
source_context: *"Can explode."

statement: Threeworld's atmosphere remains despite low surface gravity due to unknown mechanisms.
source_context: Threeworld is a tiny little planet—only about the size of Earth’s moon. But unlike our airless neighbor, Threeworld somehow has an atmosphere. How? I have no idea.

statement: Eridians lack ancient planetary naming traditions.
source_context: They didn’t have ancient people looking up at astronomical bodies and naming them after gods.

statement: Rocky does not have eyes.
source_context: He doesn’t have eyes.

statement: Rocky believes his equipment still works without light.
source_context: Rocky scuttles in his tunnel and says, 'My equipment still works.'

statement: Rocky believes humans are helpless without light.
source_context: 'Amaze. Humans helpless without light.'

statement: The narrator believes Rocky can fix machines.
source_context: Rocky seems able to do anything.

statement: Rocky believes the generator is the source of the problem.
source_context: 'Give me generator. I fix.'

statement: Rocky misunderstands human biology by assuming humans will run out of oxygen.
source_context: 'What is problem, question?'

statement: Rocky believes human memory is inadequate for navigating the ship.
source_context: 'Mmm,' he grumbles.

statement: Rocky believes the generator is the primary issue causing power loss.
source_context: 'Give me generator. I fix.'

statement: Rocky does not know the ship's orbit decay timeline.
source_context: 'How long until we die, question?'

statement: Rocky learns that Taumoeba in the fuel caused the power loss.
source_context: 'How Taumoeba get into fuel, question?'

statement: Rocky equates smell with taste, misunderstanding human sensory perception.
source_context: 'Is natural smell or chemical smell, question?'

statement: Rocky believes he can fix the generator by retrieving it.
source_context: *"Give me generator. I fix."*

statement: Rocky believes Taumoeba can be removed from the generator through sterilization.
source_context: *"I clean and sterilize. Remove all Taumoeba."*

statement: Rocky does not understand the concept of using Taumoeba to generate thrust via methane combustion.
source_context: *"No understand word after Taumoeba."*

statement: The narrator calculates the ship's maximum achievable velocity using the beetles' fuel.
source_context: The narrator types on the calculator and states the velocity.

statement: Rocky believes he can use the beetles to return to his ship.
source_context: *"Enough to get us to my ship."*

statement: The narrator realizes the beetles are self-contained and have sufficient fuel for propulsion.
source_context: The narrator concludes the beetles' design allows them to launch back to Earth.

statement: Rocky believes humans require sleep for survival.
source_context: *"Status, question?"* "Making progress," the narrator says. *"Good."*

statement: The ship's spin thrusters are inoperable due to Taumoeba contamination.
source_context: The narrator states the thrusters are full of Taumoeba poo.

statement: Rocky misunderstands human physiological needs, insisting on sleep for survival.
source_context: *"Status, question?"* "Making progress," the narrator says. *"Good."*

statement: The narrator calculates tether strength and safety margins for an EVA.
source_context: The narrator quadruple-checks tethers and states, "Should."

statement: Rocky believes he can manufacture screws to repair the ship.
source_context: The narrator questions Rocky's ability to make screws: "Um… Rocky, you can make screws, right?"

statement: The universe lazily revolves around me every twenty-five seconds.
source_context: The universe lazily revolves around me every twenty-five seconds.

statement: The beetle hatch is in the correct position and requires careful handling to avoid damage.
source_context: The beetle hatch is just where it should be. I’m going to have to be careful here. I don’t want to damage anything.

statement: The *Hail Mary* was designed as a suicide mission with pyros to blow off the hatch for beetle launch.
source_context: This was all designed to be a suicide mission. They didn’t care about the *Hail Mary* getting home. The mechanism inside has pyros to blow off this hatch.

statement: The nose cone must remain intact for aerodynamics due to relativistic effects of interstellar medium resistance.
source_context: Because of the interstellar medium... I need the nose intact.

statement: Eridian electronics are less advanced than Earth technology.
source_context: Eridian electronics not as advanced as Earth's. Dead Astrophage have water... oxygen and heat create burn marks.

statement: Rocky can work efficiently under pressure when needed.
source_context: Rocky passes the three modified beetles... You mount on hull, aim forty-five degrees...

statement: Humans have multiple hands (e.g., 'second hand', 'third hand') for tasks.
source_context: *‘You mount on hull,’* he says. *‘Aim forty-five degrees...’* ‘Understand.’ I sigh. Another EVA...

statement: Combustion in space requires oxygen, which is absent, making burn marks impossible.
source_context: ‘Burn marks are odd... How did it burn?’ *‘Theory: Many Astrophage... water and heat become hydrogen and oxygen.’*

statement: Eridians use radio for communication instead of sound-based methods.
source_context: *‘Communication established. All beetles function...’*

statement: Rocky can bypass ship controls by directly applying voltage to circuits.
source_context: *‘Communication established. All beetles function...’*

statement: Rocky understands conservation of rotational inertia and calculates ship spin based on previous events.
source_context: In fact, it’ll spin exactly as fast as it was when Rocky had to save me last time. We haven’t gained or lost any inertia in that time.

statement: Rocky acknowledges human vulnerability to high g-forces but does not fully grasp their physiological effects.
source_context: *"You are not healthy!"* Rocky squeaks. *"Undo this. We make new plan."

statement: Rocky recognizes the beetles' role in ship control but acknowledges their limitations in powering the ship.
source_context: *"Rotation rate is zero,"* he says. *"Beetles hard to control. Correction: Beetles easy to control. Ship powered by beetles hard to control."

statement: Rocky accepts the necessity of mathematical calculations for navigation.
source_context: *"Good,"* he says after the narrator explains needing to calculate thrust duration and angle.

statement: Rocky possesses expertise in engineering solutions for the *Hail Mary* ship's structural integrity.
source_context: Rocky assures me that the ship can now handle full thrust from the beetles and I don’t doubt him for a second. The guy knows engineering.

statement: Rocky understood the need to zero out rotation to control the *Hail Mary*’s beetle thrust alignment.
source_context: Rocky was mindful of that when he zeroed out our rotation. Now we have that under control and I can do EVAs in zero g like God intended.

statement: Rocky rapidly fabricated xenonite struts to reinforce the *Hail Mary*’s beetle attachment points.
source_context: I 3-D print a model of the *Hail Mary*’s internal skeleton and give it to Rocky for his perusal. In under an hour, he not only has a solution but has fabricated the xenonite struts to implement it.

statement: Rocky zeroed out their rotation to control the *Hail Mary*’s spin.
source_context: Rocky was mindful of that when he zeroed out our rotation. Now we have that under control and I can do EVAs in zero g like God intended.

statement: Rocky fabricated xenonite struts to reinforce the *Hail Mary*’s beetles.
source_context: I 3-D print a model of the *Hail Mary*’s internal skeleton and give it to Rocky for his perusal. In under an hour, he not only has a solution but has fabricated the xenonite struts to implement it.

statement: Rocky’s engineering expertise ensures the *Hail Mary* can handle full thrust.
source_context: Rocky assures me that the ship can handle full thrust, and I don’t doubt him.

statement: Rocky is qualified to manage the *Hail Mary*’s engine controls.
source_context: Rocky’s a ship’s engineer. Who better to run our makeshift engines?

statement: Rocky previously executed the delicate process of zeroing out rotation.
source_context: The narrator refers to Rocky’s past action as proven: 'You’re a coward and you always have been. You abandoned a promising scientific career...'

statement: Taumoeba survive when not in Adrian air. Taumoeba stronger than Erid life—stronger than Earth life.
source_context: Rocky: 'Taumoeba survive when not in Adrian air. Taumoeba stronger than Erid life—stronger than Earth life.'

statement: Nitrogen is unexpected and lethal to Taumoeba.
source_context: Rocky: 'Nitrogen…unexpected. Nitrogen kill Taumoeba.'

statement: Eridian bodies use heat to kill diseases, lacking an immune system.
source_context: Rocky: 'Eridians have no immune system. We use heat to kill disease.'

statement: Astrophage and Taumoeba originate from the same biosphere.
source_context: Rocky: 'Astrophage and Taumoeba from same biosphere.'

statement: Threeworld air, Venus air, and Taumoeba cannot be altered to coexist.
source_context: Rocky: 'Hopeless. Cannot change Threeworld air. Cannot change Venus air. Cannot change Taumoeba. Hopeless.'

statement: Threeworld air is eight percent nitrogen. Cannot change Threeworld air.
source_context: *"Situation bad. Threeworld air is eight percent nitrogen."*

statement: Venus’s air is 3.5 percent nitrogen. Cannot change Venus air.
source_context: *"Situation bad. Threeworld air is eight percent nitrogen."*

statement: Eridian body is closed. Only opening happens when eat or lay egg. Disease can only get into body through wound.
source_context: *"Eridian body is closed,"* he explains. *"Only opening happen when eat or lay egg. After opening seals, area inside made very hot inside with hot blood for long time. Kill any disease."*

statement: Antibiotics and cures for diseases in nature are incomprehensible.
source_context: *"No understand,"* he says when asked about cures for diseases in nature.

statement: Evolution through natural selection (Taumoeba breeding for nitrogen resistance).
source_context: *"Good good,"* he says after explaining aggressive nitrogen spacing for Taumoeba-06.

statement: Eridian food contains heavy metals (thallium) and is considered healthy.
source_context: *"Why would ship have name, question?"*

statement: Real food equates to taste; non-real food lacks value.
source_context: *"Why does ship have name but chair no have name, question?"*

statement: Nitrogen tolerance tracking uses pressure as a constant for simplicity.
source_context: *"What spacing, question?"*... "I’m being aggressive—0.05 percent increments."

statement: Ship positioning around Tau Ceti ensures stable orbit for beacon flashes.
source_context: *"You in control now."*... *"Next flash is three minutes, seven seconds."*

statement: Ship naming conventions are unnecessary or incomprehensible.
source_context: *"Why would ship have name, question?"*

statement: Rocky calculates a 37-second interval until the flash.
source_context: *"Understand. Thirty-seven seconds until flash."

statement: Rocky does not comprehend human naming conventions for objects.
source_context: *"Why would ship have name, question?"

statement: Rocky believes ships do not require names.
source_context: *"Ship."

statement: Rocky identifies the ship's name as 'Blip-A'.
source_context: *"That is what I said. Flash in ten seconds."

statement: Rocky confirms the *Hail Mary* is aligned with the telescope angle.
source_context: *"Angle correct."

statement: Rocky reports no detection on his texture screen.
source_context: *"I no detect anything on-screen."

statement: Rocky calculates the distance to the *Blip-A* as at least 10,000 kilometers.
source_context: *"Too far for my radar to see. At least ten thousand kilometers."

statement: Rocky accepts a standard acceleration rate of 15 meters per second squared.
source_context: *"Two hundred second thrust. Begin now."

statement: Rocky believes the creation of Taumoeba-35 is a scientific breakthrough after many generations.
source_context: *“Taumoeba-35!”* Rocky says. *“Took many many generations but finally success!”*

statement: Rocky is trusted to perform engineering tasks, even hypothetical open-heart surgery.
source_context: He trust Rocky to do any engineering task. Heck, if he wanted to do open-heart surgery on me, I’d probably let him.

statement: Rocky is constructing an Earth electricity unit to convert Eridian prime-sequence electric amplitude to Earth's direct-current system.
source_context: *“This is Earth electricity unit.”*...*“Convert from Eridian prime-sequence electric amplitude to inefficient Earth direct-current system.”*

statement: Rocky misunderstands the narrator's laptop as a 'portable thinking machine' capable of storing Wikipedia data.
source_context: The narrator assumes Rocky thinks they have terabyte drives and can copy Wikipedia.

statement: Rocky believes the laptop requires life-support systems to function in Eridian air.
source_context: *“You want xenonite patch for hole now, question?”*...The narrator assumes Rocky's system has redundant backups.

statement: Rocky knows enough English to understand the narrator's explanation of written language.
source_context: The narrator notes Rocky 'knows enough English' to learn written language.

statement: Rocky believes the narrator's laptop is a valuable gift for Earth scientists.
source_context: The narrator assumes Rocky thinks Earth scientists will want xenonite.

statement: Rocky calculates nitrogen partial pressure requirements for Taumoeba sterilization.
source_context: The narrator explains Rocky knows 3.5% at 0.02 atmospheres kills natural Taumoeba.

statement: Rocky believes ammonia from the *Blip-A* life support system can assist with nitrogen.
source_context: *“You have enough nitrogen, question? I can give ammonia...”*

statement: The narrator calculates precise nitrogen gas quantities needed to sterilize fuel bays.
source_context: The narrator explains needing 'a few grams of nitrogen gas' to kill Taumoeba.

statement: Rocky believes the narrator's method will ensure fuel bay sterility after Astrophage addition.
source_context: The narrator checks fuel bays expecting no Taumoeba left.

statement: Rocky uses handholds to navigate Fuel Bay Four.
source_context: I use the handholds to get to Fuel Bay Four...

statement: Xenonite is effective for pressurized gas containers.
source_context: Xenonite makes for some pretty darn good pressurized gas containers.

statement: Rocky cleans and reseals fuel bays.
source_context: My fuel bays are all freshly cleaned and resealed...

statement: Astrophage was previously valuable but is now just energy.
source_context: I remember when 'a few kilograms of Astrophage' would have been a godsend...now it's just energy.

statement: Rocky believes insufficient cleaning caused Taumoeba survival.
source_context: I probably didn’t clean them well enough...

statement: Rocky can receive radio signals from the *Blip-A*.
source_context: He can always hear me.

statement: Nitrogen's role in Taumoeba survival is an unresolved mystery.
source_context: Someday we find out why nitrogen was problem.

statement: Rocky believes his presence on the *Blip-A* is unnecessary.
source_context: What good could I do aboard the *Blip-A* anyway?

statement: Rocky assumes fuel lines are infected due to prior contamination.
source_context: It’s safe to assume the fuel lines...will also be infected.

statement: Rocky can construct storage tanks from any strong material.
source_context: Don’t need xenonite. Any strong material will do...

statement: Rocky describes the alloy as a 'metal stew'.
source_context: This is a metal stew.

statement: Breeder tanks have nitrogen levels ranging from 0.25% to 8%.
source_context: spacing is 0.25 percent...some breeder tanks actually have 8 percent or more nitrogen...

statement: Rocky believes the breeder tank process is inefficient.
source_context: You are slow.

statement: Rocky has limited food supplies on his ship.
source_context: I don’t have that much food.

statement: Breeder Tanks Nine and Ten are excited about their progress.
source_context: *"Apologies. I am excited. Breeder Tanks Nine and Ten!"*

statement: The ship's acceleration of 15 meters per second squared requires verifying tank integrity.
source_context: *"Danger, question? Your ship accelerate at 15 meters per second per second. Will tanks hold, question?"*

statement: Humans leak water excessively and are inefficient compared to Eridians.
source_context: *"We keep inside. Closed system. Some inefficiencies inside, but we get all water we need from food. Humans leak! Gross."*

statement: All experiments must use identical conditions (gases, pressure, temperature, radiation, light).
source_context: *"Exact same gases in each test. Same pressure. Same temperature. Same death 'radiation' from space. Same light from nearby star. Same same same."*

statement: Human-Eridian collaboration will save all planets.
source_context: *"Human and Eridian work together, save everyone!"*

statement: Eridians cannot see stars because they are too far away.
source_context: *"We cannot see the stars. They are too far."*

statement: Friendship between humans and Eridians will persist despite separation.
source_context: *"You will miss me, question? I will miss you. You are friend."*

statement: Astrophage technology will enable interplanetary visits between species.
source_context: *"We save planets. Then we have Astrophage technology. Visit each other."*

statement: Earth is almost the same distance from Tau Ceti as Erid.
source_context: *"But Earth is almost same distance from Tau Ceti, and you will take four years, question?"*

statement: Human time dilation experiences are equivalent to Eridian ones despite differing ship acceleration rates.
source_context: *"You have explained before, but again…why, question?"* I explain about faster acceleration and time compression.

statement: Astrophage technology enables interstellar travel between Erid and human worlds.
source_context: *"We save planets. Then we have Astrophage technology. Visit each other."*

statement: Human-provided laptop contains centuries of technological advancement for Eridian scientists.
source_context: *"Thank you for laptop. Centuries of human technology all for our scientists to learn about."*

statement: Testing life-support systems requires integrating xenonite materials with human tech.
source_context: *"That is stupid question."* (referring to laptop testing in life-support system)

statement: Human time dilation calculations require explaining relativity concepts to Eridian scientists.
source_context: *"Not understand."* I explain relativity is in the laptop for their scientists.

statement: Using light as a propellant could enable communication between Earth and Erid via massive releases of Petrova light.
source_context: Maybe that’s something we could use in the future. Maybe Earth and Erid could communicate with massive releases of Petrova light thanks to Astrophage.

statement: The distance between Earth and 40 Eridani is sixteen light-years.
source_context: 40 Eridani is sixteen light-years away from Earth. So if we sent a message like 'Hey, how ya doin’?' it would be thirty-two years before we got their reply.

statement: Relative velocities between Earth and Erid will cause red-shift in light from Petrovascope observations.
source_context: It won’t be the Petrova wavelength anymore when it gets to me.

statement: Calculating relativistic math for red-shift tracking is a pathetic endeavor.
source_context: Would I do a ridiculous amount of relativistic math...? Wouldn’t that be kind of pathetic?

statement: The *Hail Mary*’s water system is a closed-loop system with no liquid storage for long-term use.
source_context: The water system of the *Hail Mary* is a closed loop. Water goes into me, it comes out of me in various ways, and then it’s purified and reused.

statement: Eridian steel can be cut by Earth's diamond saws and analyzed for replication.
source_context: Earth can cut it open with a diamond saw. And hey, they’ll probably analyze it to learn how to make their own.

statement: The smell of dead Astrophage indicates Taumoeba have escaped containment.
source_context: I know that smell. It’s the smell of dead, rotting Astrophage. The Taumoeba are loose again.

statement: A single sealed container is necessary to prevent air leakage in Taumoeba farms.
source_context: He insisted the whole farm be a single, completely sealed container. Probably a good idea.

statement: Beetles require 60 kilograms of Astrophage each for full fueling.
source_context: But they only need 60 kilograms of Astrophage each to be full.

statement: The beetles' guidance system adjusts acceleration based on fuel levels.
source_context: They know their location in space by looking at the stars, and if they have less fuel than they expected to have, they taper their acceleration down as needed.

statement: The BOCOA is still hot. That means there’s a lot of living Astrophage still in there.
source_context:
I leap from the stool, but I don’t have a plan.

“Okay, don’t panic,” I tell myself. “Think clearly. Then act.”

The BOCOA is still hot. That means there’s a lot of living Astrophage still in there.

statement: The only Taumoeba aboard are in the sealed mini-farms on the beetles and the sealed, xenonite breeder tanks.
source_context:
No. No time for science questions. I can speculate on the cause later. Right now I have an engineering problem. I wish Rocky were here.

I always wish Rocky were here.

statement: Taumoeba-82.5 can handle 8.25 percent nitrogen at 0.02 atmospheres but definitely cannot handle 100 percent nitrogen at 0.33 atmospheres.
source_context: I don’t know how the Taumoeba got out, but I need them dead. Taumoeba-82.5 can handle 8.25 percent nitrogen at 0.02 atmospheres. Maybe a little higher. But it definitely can’t handle 100 percent nitrogen at the crew compartment’s 0.33 atmospheres.

statement: The ship’s life-support system has manual overpressure valves that will vent excess pressure into space.
source_context: I don’t remember all the details about the life-support system, but I know it has manual overpressure valves. The ship simply will not allow more than 0.33 atmospheres.

statement: Replacing air with nitrogen will kill all Taumoeba in the system.
source_context: I want 100 percent nitrogen in here. I want to make this ship so utterly toxic... that any Taumoeba left will die.

statement: The emergency airlock valve’s size directly correlates with the time required to depressurize the ship.
source_context: The emergency valve on the airlock is 4 centimeters across... it took twenty minutes for the ship’s air pressure to drop.

statement: 0.33 atmospheres of nitrogen is safe for human respiration.
source_context: I’d be perfectly comfortable if I took this EVA suit off. I’d breathe without any problems.

statement: Jettisoning the BOCOA vat is a necessary sacrifice to prevent mission contamination.
source_context: I probably could have saved the surviving Astrophage... but why take the chance?

statement: Rocky and I learned that Taumoeba can only last about a week without food before it starves to death.
source_context: Rocky and I learned that Taumoeba can only last about a week without food before it starves to death.

statement: Rocky knows what he’s doing, and he knows all about Eridian steel.
source_context: Rocky knows what he’s doing, and he knows all about Eridian steel.

statement: Rocky never makes mistakes. Not when it comes to creating things.
source_context: Rocky never makes mistakes. Not when it comes to creating things.

statement: Rocky’s tunnel system
source_context: Rocky’s tunnel system

statement: Rocky’s 29 atmospheres of pressure
source_context: Rocky’s 29 atmospheres of pressure

statement: I know the answer. I don’t want to admit it to myself. But I know the answer.
source_context: I know the answer. I don’t want to admit it to myself. But I know the answer.

statement: Rocky’s workshop
source_context: Rocky’s workshop

statement: Life-forms don’t evolve traits for no reason.
source_context: Life-forms don’t evolve traits for no reason. Taumoeba lives in the upper atmosphere. Why would it develop the ability to work its way through dense molecular structures? What evolutionary reason could there be to—

statement: Taumoeba from Adrian can navigate xenonite, a technological invention from Erid, without an apparent evolutionary reason.
source_context: How could Taumoeba, from the planet Adrian, know how to carefully navigate its way through xenonite, a technological invention from the planet Erid? It does not make sense.

statement: Taumoeba-82.5 can permeate xenonite but cannot penetrate plastic, epoxy, glass, or metal.
source_context: The xenonite-covered Astrophage in the Taumoeba-82.5 experiment is gone. The plastic-covered Astrophage remains unchanged... Taumoeba can’t get through ordinary plastic. It can’t get through epoxy resin. It can’t get through glass. It can’t get through metal.

statement: Natural Taumoeba cannot penetrate xenonite, while Taumoeba-82.5 can.
source_context: The xenonite-covered Astrophage in the Taumoeba-82.5 experiment is gone... Meanwhile in the other experiment, both Astrophage samples are unharmed.

statement: Evolution can produce unintended consequences, such as nitrogen-resistant Taumoeba also gaining xenonite-penetration abilities.
source_context: I made a strain of Taumoeba that could survive nitrogen. But evolution doesn’t care what I want... they figured out how to hide from nitrogen by sneaking into the xenonite itself!

statement: Rocky’s xenonite-based ship design is a critical vulnerability for Taumoeba.
source_context: Rocky has the same strain of Taumoeba aboard his ship... All critical bulkheads of his ship, including the fuel tanks, are made of xenonite. There’s nothing standing between his Taumoeba and his fuel.

statement: Taumoeba can survive in a Venusian atmosphere without relying on xenonite.
source_context: It’ll still do its thing on Venus and Threeworld. Everything’s fine.

statement: Rocky’s ship design can be repurposed by replacing xenonite with metal for Taumoeba containment.
source_context: I’ll make a big farm out of metal... I just need to put it on a different car.

statement: Rocky’s ship is non-functional and its engine flare has ceased.
source_context: I’ve been watching his engine flare every day for the past month. Now it’s gone.

statement: The *Blip-A* should be at a precise location down to milli-arc-second accuracy.
source_context: I know right where it should be. Down to the milli-arc-second.

statement: Rocky’s fuel compartments made of xenonite are insufficient to prevent Taumoeba consumption.
source_context: He’s smart, so he surely has the fuel compartmentalized. But those compartments are made of xenonite, right? Yeah.

statement: Rocky would fix his ship if damaged, as he is capable and works quickly.
source_context: If the ship were damaged, he’d fix it. Rocky moves fast.

statement: Launching beetles to Earth and then traveling to Erid is impossible due to food shortages.
source_context: But he’s got energy. Life support. Food enough to last him a long, long time (original crew of twenty-three...).

statement: Rocky is actively working on a solution despite his dire situation.
source_context: Maybe he’ll make a radio signal... Rocky will know that too. So there’s no point.

statement: The narrator believes their modified radar system (using spin drives and Petrovascope) can detect Rocky.
source_context: I can throw 900 terawatts of IR light out the back... I can’t have the Petrovascope and engines on at the same time.

statement: Rocky’s ship has no fuel remaining, leading to its non-functionality.
source_context: There’s just no way... Some back-of-the-napkin math tells me that even with Earth’s radio technology... the strength of that signal at Erid would be way less than background noise.

statement: The vastness of space and error margins in tracking Rocky’s position make rescue efforts challenging.
source_context: Space is three-dimensional... I’ve only searched one flat slice of the area.

statement: Generating a detectable radio signal from Rocky’s ship is infeasible due to distance and energy limitations.
source_context: But... no. There’s just no way... the strength of that signal at Erid would be way less than background noise.

statement: The searcher assumes radar can detect objects at 4,000 kilometers despite Eridian technology potentially operating under different physical principles.
source_context: I’m 4,000 kilometers away—the very edge of radar range.

statement: The searcher believes Rocky’s ship (Blip-A) is on a hyperbolic trajectory escaping Tau Ceti’s gravity.
source_context: The *Hail Mary* is on a hyperbolic trajectory. That means I’m not in orbit at all. I’m on an escape vector, leaving Tau Ceti’s gravity influence entirely.

statement: Rocky knows the profile of the *Blip-A* is a triangle shape.
source_context: It’s the *Blip-A.* I know the profile well.

statement: Rocky believes Eridian and human proteins are sufficiently similar to allow consumption of Eridian food.
source_context: You no can eat Erid life. You no can eat Earth life. But you can eat both? No, I think not.

statement: Rocky believes the narrator cannot die from starvation.
source_context: You no can die. You are friend.

statement: Rocky believes Eridians may send another ship to rescue him in the future.
source_context: Erid maybe send another ship someday.

statement: Rocky knows Taumoeba-82.5 can infiltrate xenonite over time.
source_context: Make sure no Taumoeba-82.5 get into Hail Mary.

statement: Eridian food is toxic due to heavy metals present in their ecology.
source_context: I hold up my hands. "It’s not just bad for me. It will kill me. Your whole ecology uses heavy metals all over the place. Most of them are toxic to me. I’d die immediately."

statement: Eridian and human biology share common proteins, chemicals, and sugars, making their food potentially edible.
source_context: *"Eat Erid food. We evolve from same life. We use same proteins. Same chemicals. Same sugars. Must work!"*

statement: Taumoeba may be edible due to lacking heavy metals and having Earth-like biological features.
source_context: Can I eat Taumoeba?... It’s not Astrophage. It’s not 96 degrees. It’s just an amoeba from another planet. It won’t have heavy metals...

statement: Astrophage is inedible due to its high temperature and alien cell membrane structure.
source_context: "I can’t eat that! It’s ninety-six degrees all the time! It would burn me alive. Plus, I doubt my digestive enzymes would even work on its weird cell membrane."

statement: The Eridians are fantastic hosts and will keep him alive due to his role in saving their planet.
source_context: The Eridians... agreed to do whatever it takes to keep me alive. After all, I played a critical role in saving their planet.

statement: The *Hail Mary* probe was a viable solution to save Earth from Astrophage.
source_context: The Eridians could stock it up with food and supplies... but so far I haven’t taken them up on it.

statement: Earth is sixteen light-years away from Erid.
source_context: There’s no way to communicate with Earth. It’s sixteen light-years away.

statement: Eridians lack understanding of human biology and visual language (e.g., interpreting 'fist-bump' as a gesture).
source_context: He holds a balled claw against the xenonite... I’ve come to realize is a smile.

statement: The sun's return to normal brightness confirms Earth's habitability.
source_context: Until a minute ago I didn’t even know if Earth was still habitable.

statement: Time dilation calculations show the journey to Earth would take less than one Earth year.
source_context: The trip is long... but Rocky... that news about Sol…it makes my whole life have meaning.

statement: Eridians can create any object requested by humans.
source_context: They made me a wristwatch. They make anything I ask for.

statement: The group mind of Eridians (thrums) is an accurate description of their culture.
source_context: Each one is no more than thirty Earth years old... again, Eridian culture is complicated.

statement: Astrophage seeded life on both Earth and Erid.
source_context: Some ancestor of Astrophage seeded Earth and Erid with life billions of years ago.

statement: Humanity's survival on Earth depended on collective effort to implement the *Hail Mary* solution.
source_context: They were able to collect the beetles... implement a solution. A solution that would have involved a probe going to Venus.
